speaker_role: independent counselor (Jen Foran, college counselor at Campus Bound)
commercial_incentive: yes; Campus Bound is a paid college counseling service, and the video invites viewers to book a consultation
key_insights: Distinguishes four letter types: school counselor, core academic teacher (required by most schools), non-core/elective teacher (generally discouraged except for arts/music applicants), and outside recommenders (coaches, employers)
Outside recommenders must be personally invited by the student via the Common App portal; high schools cannot submit these letters themselves under FERPA rules
Most colleges read exactly two core-academic-teacher letters, so advises requesting two even when only one is technically required
Strongly recommends teacher letters come specifically from junior-year teachers, as the most recent relevant academic representation
A student-completed 'brag sheet' is often what most determines counselor-letter quality, since counselors have large caseloads and limited one-on-one time
Advises against defaulting to a strict 'one STEM, one non-STEM' teacher split if two same-subject teachers know the student far better; letter quality matters more than subject-matching
notable_or_distinctive: explicitly explains the FERPA-driven procedural rule that high schools cannot submit outside-recommender letters themselves, requiring the student to personally invite them via Common App, a detail not commonly covered elsewhere
reliability_notes: presenter is a paid counselor; advice is standard, non-controversial counseling guidance, though some claims (e.g., 'most colleges read two') are generalized from firm experience rather than cited data
